### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Summary

OpenClaw 2026.3.8 sends the full provider/model ref (e.g., google/gemini-2.5-pro) as the model ID to the Google Generative AI API's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The API expects only gemini-2.5-pro and returns a 404 because models/google/gemini-2.5-pro does not exist.
This is a regression — the same configuration works correctly on 2026.3.3.
Related issues: #795 (identical bug in 2026.1.x), #16010 (NVIDIA prefix stripping issue)
Environment

OpenClaw version: 2026.3.8 (Docker: ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw:latest)
Previous working version: 2026.3.3
OS: Ubuntu (Hetzner VPS)
Install method: Docker Compose

### Steps to reproduce

Steps to reproduce

Configure Google provider with the OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

json"models": {
  "providers": {
    "google": {
      "baseUrl": "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/",
      "apiKey": "...",
      "models": [
        { "id": "gemini-2.5-pro", "name": "Gemini 2.5 Pro" }
      ]
    }
  }
}

Configure an agent with "model": "google/gemini-2.5-pro"
Send any message to the agent

### Expected behavior

OpenClaw splits google/gemini-2.5-pro into provider=google and model=gemini-2.5-pro, then sends only gemini-2.5-pro as the model ID to the Google API.
Actual behavior
OpenClaw sends google/gemini-2.5-pro as the model ID. Google API responds:
json{

Ubuntu

docker


_No response_

issue:
#### Issue #557: Alpine package depends on systemd

_Original issue by edward-shen on 2023-05-25T04:04:35.000Z_

### Description

Hey folks!

I was thinking of trying out Vikunja on a lxc container. I was able to fetch the `.apk` file but quickly became stuck:

Repro steps:

```
# wget https://dl.vikunja.io/api/0.20.4/vikunja-0.20.4-x86_64.apk
# apk add --allow-untrusted vikunja-0.20.4-x86_64.apk 
ERROR: unable to select packages:
  systemd (no such package):
    required by: vikunja-0.20.4[systemd]
```

Alpine Linux uses [OpenRC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenRC) as its init system, so having a dependency on `systemd` here is incorrect. As far as I can tell, there's no way to actually install `systemd` on an Alpine Linux system.

I can use a different base image as a workaround, but that really inflates the container size so I'd rather not if possible.

### Vikunja Frontend Version

n/a

### Vikunja API Version

0.20.4

### Browser and version

_No response_

### Can you reproduce the bug on the Vikunja demo site?

n/a

_No response_



[Original issue on Gitea](https://kolaente.dev/vikunja/vikunja/issues/1530)

If you want to build a container with it, why don't you use the binary directly? (I've never done anything with LXC, don't know what's the best practice there?)

Hi! LXC is just how I set it up -- the issue is independent of LXC or containers in general. 

I raised this issue because Vikunja offers an Alpine linux package [here](https://vikunja.io/download/) but the Alpine linux package doesn't work on a vanilla install of Alpine linux, which felt like a bug.

The primary benefit of having using the APK would be integrating with the init system to daemonize Vikunja without relying on other tools (which would kinda be against one of alpine linux's features: being small).

pr_title: fix: detect REPLAN-TRIGGER.md in deriveState for triage-initiated replans
issue:
#### Issue #1701: Manual /gsd triage replan is ignored by /gsd next and advances to the next slice

## Problem
Manual `/gsd capture` → `/gsd triage` can recommend `replan` for a completed slice, but the next `/gsd next` still advances into the next slice instead of entering slice replanning. In the reproduced case, triage recommended replanning `S01`, but `/gsd next` dispatched `research-slice` for `S02`.

## Root Cause
There are two linked defects in the triage → dispatch path.

1. **Manual `/gsd triage` only classifies captures; it does not execute the resulting resolution.**
   `commands-handlers.js:127-163` dispatches a `gsd-triage` session, but the resolution executor only runs in the auto-mode post-unit path when the completed unit type is exactly `triage-captures`.

```js
// commands-handlers.js:127-163
export async function handleTriage(ctx, pi, basePath) {
  ...
  pi.sendMessage({
    customType: "gsd-triage",
    content: ...,
  }, { triggerTurn: true });
}

// auto-post-unit.js:226-239
if (s.currentUnit.type === "triage-captures") {
  const triageResult = executeTriageResolutions(s.basePath, mid, sid);
}
```

Because manual triage never enters that `triage-captures` unit type, captures can be marked `resolved` + `classification: replan` in `.gsd/CAPTURES.md` without any replan trigger actually being applied.

2. **The written replan trigger is not consumed by the state machine.**
   `triage-resolution.js:64-79` writes `Sxx-REPLAN-TRIGGER.md`, but `state.js:606-647` does not read that trigger. Instead it only enters `replanning-slice` when a completed task summary has `blocker_discovered: true` and `Sxx-REPLAN.md` does not exist.

```js
// triage-resolution.js:64-79
const triggerPath = join(basePath, ".gsd", "milestones", mid, "slices", sid, `${sid}-REPLAN-TRIGGER.md`);
writeFileSync(triggerPath, content, "utf-8");

// state.js:618-628
if (summary.frontmatter.blocker_discovered) {
  blockerTaskId = ct.id;
}
const replanFile = resolveSliceFile(basePath, activeMilestone.id, activeSlice.id, "REPLAN");
if (!replanFile) {
  return { phase: 'replanning-slice', ... };
}
```

Once the previous slice is already marked done, `state.js:483-492` selects the first incomplete slice as `activeSlice`, so `/gsd next` naturally advances into the next slice and never revisits the triaged slice.

## Expected Behavior
After manual `/gsd triage` confirms a `replan` classification:

- GSD should persist a scheduler-visible replan intent that `/gsd next` can see.
- The persisted signal should identify the target slice explicitly, including when that slice is already marked complete.
- `/gsd next` should prioritize dispatching `replan-slice` for that target slice before advancing to the next incomplete slice.

Concrete fix suggestion:

1. Extract triage-resolution application into a shared path used by both manual `/gsd triage` and auto-mode `triage-captures`.
2. Unify the replan protocol so the writer and reader use the same artifact (either consume `*-REPLAN-TRIGGER.md` in `deriveState()`, or stop writing it and persist the exact state signal `deriveState()` already understands).
3. Persist `targetSlice` in `.gsd/CAPTURES.md` and let dispatch prefer pending replan targets over the default “first incomplete slice” selection.

## Environment
- GSD version: 2.40.0
- Model: gpt-5.4
- Unit: `research/slice-M002-28g94x-S02` (incorrectly dispatched after manual triage recommended replanning `S01`)

## Reproduction Context
Phase flow in the captured run:
1. `run/uat-M002-28g94x-S01`
2. `reassess/roadmap-M002-28g94x-S01`
3. User manually ran `/gsd capture` and `/gsd triage`, which classified the capture as `replan`
4. User then ran `/gsd next`
5. GSD dispatched `research/slice-M002-28g94x-S02` instead of re-entering `replan-slice` for `S01`

## Forensic Evidence
- `.gsd/CAPTURES.md` shows the capture resolved with `Classification: replan`, but no execution marker was written.
- No `S01-REPLAN-TRIGGER.md` or `S01-REPLAN.md` existed after triage.
- Activity logs show the next dispatched unit was `.gsd/activity/009-research-slice-M002-28g94x-S02.jsonl`.
- The prior completed unit was `.gsd/activity/008-reassess-roadmap-M002-28g94x-S01.jsonl`.
- Current state after the bad transition shows `Active Slice: S02` and `Phase: planning`, confirming the scheduler advanced instead of honoring the triage result.

---

pr_title: feat: implement UPDATE DML operation for Delta Lake
issue:
#### Issue #1472: UPDATE and DELETE should rewrite/remove only touched files for non-partition predicates

https://github.com/lakehq/sail/pull/1462
MERGE and UPDATE/DELETE have different complexity profiles:

- MERGE is relationally complex, so logical expansion is the right layer.
- UPDATE/DELETE are relationally simple, but storage-path optimization is the hard part.

Current gap: UPDATE/DELETE may still rewrite/remove candidate files that are not truly touched by row-level predicates.

- Solution 1: logical pre-expansion
- Solution 2: apply two-pass physical plan to UPDATE/DELETE 

This issue currently only occurs in the delta lake integration.

issue:
#### Issue #356: Replace tibdex/github-app-token with actions/create-github-app-token

# Overview

The action `tibdex/github-app-token` is archived, so we have to change to use a different action. The action `actions/create-github-app-token` offered a similar functionality.

# Steps

* List the .github/actions and .github/workflows using `tibdex/github-app-token`
* Replace `tibdex/github-app-token` with the same configuration using `actions/create-github-app-token` for all the .github/actions and workflows.
* Link the PR to this issue as closed by the PR.

# Example

The following configuration with `tibdex/github-app-token`

```yaml
      - name: Get token
        id: get_token
        uses: tibdex/github-app-token@3beb63f4bd073e61482598c45c71c1019b59b73a
        with:
          app_id: ${{ secrets.OBS_AUTOMATION_APP_ID }}
          private_key: ${{ secrets.OBS_AUTOMATION_APP_PEM }}
          repositories: >-
            [
              "oblt-framework",
              "observability-test-environments"
            ]
          permissions: >-
            {
              "contents": "write",
              "pull_requests": "write",
              "members": "read"
            }
```

it is replaced by the following configuration with `actions/create-github-app-token`

```yaml
    - name: Get token from GitHub App
      id: get_token
      uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v2
      with:
        app-id: ${{ secrets.OBS_AUTOMATION_APP_ID }}
        private-key: ${{ secrets.OBS_AUTOMATION_APP_PEM }}
        permission-contents: write
        permission-pull-requests: write
        permission-members: read
        repositories: |
          oblt-framework
          observability-test-environments
```

#### Issue #3311: [refactor] 🔧 Semantic Function Clustering Analysis - Refactoring Opportunities # 🔧 Semantic Function Clustering Analysis *Analysis of repository: githubnext/gh-aw* ## Executive Summary Analyzed **180 non-test Go source files** across 8 packages, cataloging **1,000+ functions** to identify refactoring opportunities through semantic clustering and duplicate detection. The analysis revealed significant opportunities for improved code organization: - **40+ validation functions** scattered across 10 different files (should be consolidated) - **104 parse functions** across 47 files showing inconsistent organization - **30+ 'is' helper functions** spread across 11 files in workflow package alone - **15+ 'extract' helper functions** scattered across 15 files - **Multiple URL/repo parsing functions** with similar implementations in cli package - **String sanitization functions** with different naming but similar purpose **Key Finding**: While the `create_*.go` file organization pattern is excellent, validation, parsing, and helper functions lack consistent organization, leading to scattered functionality that could benefit from consolidation.
Full Analysis Report ## Codebase Structure ### Packages Overview | Package | Files | Primary Purpose | |---------|-------|----------------| | pkg/workflow | 108 | Workflow compilation, validation, execution | | pkg/cli | 60 | CLI commands and user interactions | | pkg/parser | 6 | Frontmatter, schema, YAML parsing | | pkg/console | 3 | Console output formatting | | pkg/workflow/pretty | 1 | Pretty printing utilities | | pkg/timeutil | 1 | Time formatting utilities | | pkg/logger | 1 | Logging utilities | | pkg/constants | 1 | Constant definitions | **Total**: 181 files (180 non-test Go files analyzed) ## Function Clustering Analysis ### Well-Organized Patterns ✅ #### 1. Create Functions (Excellent Organization) **Pattern**: One file per creation entity Files following this pattern: - `pkg/workflow/create_issue.go` - Issue creation - `pkg/workflow/create_discussion.go` - Discussion creation - `pkg/workflow/create_pull_request.go` - PR creation - `pkg/workflow/create_agent_task.go` - Agent task creation - `pkg/workflow/create_code_scanning_alert.go` - Alert creation - `pkg/workflow/create_pr_review_comment.go` - Review comment creation **Analysis**: ✅ This is exemplary organization. Each creation function has its own dedicated file, making the codebase easy to navigate and maintain. #### 2. Update Functions Files following this pattern: - `pkg/workflow/update_issue.go` - Issue updates **Analysis**: ✅ Consistent with create pattern, though fewer update operations exist. ### Problematic Patterns ⚠️ #### 3. +// Package workflow provides JavaScript bundler validation for agentic workflows.
+//
+// # JavaScript Bundler Validation
+//
+// This file validates bundled JavaScript to ensure that all local module dependencies
+// have been properly inlined during the bundling process. This prevents runtime errors
+// from missing local modules when JavaScript is executed in GitHub Actions.
+//
+// # Validation Functions
+//
+//   - validateNoLocalRequires() - Validates bundled JavaScript has no local require() statements
+//   - isInsideStringLiteralAt() - Helper to detect if a position is inside a string literal
+//
+// # Validation Pattern: Bundling Verification
+//
+// Bundler validation ensures that local require() statements are inlined:
+//   - Scans bundled JavaScript for require('./...') or require('../...') patterns
+//   - Ignores require statements inside string literals
+//   - Returns hard errors if local requires are found (indicates bundling failure)
+//   - Helps prevent runtime module-not-found errors
+//
+// # When to Add Validation Here
+//
+// Add validation to this file when:
+//   - It validates JavaScript bundling correctness
+//   - It checks for missing module dependencies
+//   - It validates CommonJS require() statement resolution
+//   - It validates JavaScript code structure
+//
+// For bundling functions, see bundler.go.
+// For general validation, see validation.go.
+// For detailed documentation, see specs/validation-architecture.md
+package workflow
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"regexp"
+	"strings"
+)
+
+// validateNoLocalRequires checks that the bundled JavaScript contains no local require() statements
+// that weren't inlined during bundling. This prevents runtime errors from missing local modules.
+// Returns an error if any local requires are found, otherwise returns nil
+func validateNoLocalRequires(bundledContent string) error {
+	// Regular expression to match local require statements
+	// Matches: require('./...') or require("../...")
+	localRequireRegex := regexp.MustCompile(`require\(['"](\.\.?/[^'"]+)['"]\)`)
+
+	lines := strings.Split(bundledContent, "\n")
+	var foundRequires []string
+
+	for lineNum, line := range lines {
+		// Check for local requires
+		matches := localRequireRegex.FindAllStringSubmatch(line, -1)
+		for _, match := range matches {
+			if len(match) > 1 {
+				requirePath := match[1]
+				// Check if this require is inside a string literal
+				matchIdx := strings.Index(line, match[0])
+				if matchIdx >= 0 && !isInsideStringLiteralAt(line, matchIdx) {
+					foundRequires = append(foundRequires, fmt.Sprintf("line %d: require('%s')", lineNum+1, requirePath))
+				}
+			}
+		}
+	}
+
+	if len(foundRequires) > 0 {
+		return fmt.Errorf("bundled JavaScript contains %d local require(s) that were not inlined:\n  %s",
+			len(foundRequires), strings.Join(foundRequires, "\n  "))
+	}
+
+	return nil
+}
+
+// isInsideStringLiteralAt checks if a position in a line is inside a string literal
+func isInsideStringLiteralAt(line string, pos int) bool {
+	// Count unescaped quotes before the position
+	singleQuoteCount := 0
+	doubleQuoteCount := 0
+	backtickCount := 0
+
+	for i := 0; i < pos && i < len(line); i++ {
+		// Count consecutive backslashes before the current character
+		backslashCount := 0
+		for j := i - 1; j >= 0 && line[j] == '\\'; j-- {
+			backslashCount++
+		}
+
+		// If odd number of backslashes, the current character is escaped
+		if backslashCount%2 == 1 {
+			continue
+		}
+
+		switch line[i] {
+		case '\'':
+			singleQuoteCount++
+		case '"':
+			doubleQuoteCount++
+		case '`':
+			backtickCount++
+		}
+	}
+
+	// If any quote count is odd, we're inside that type of string literal
+	return singleQuoteCount%2 == 1 || doubleQuoteCount%2 == 1 || backtickCount%2 == 1
+}

+// Package workflow provides NPM package validation for agentic workflows.
+//
+// # NPM Package Validation
+//
+// This file validates NPM package availability on the npm registry for packages
+// used with npx (Node Package Execute). Validation ensures that Node.js packages
+// specified in workflows exist and can be installed at runtime.
+//
+// # Validation Functions
+//
+//   - validateNpxPackages() - Validates npm packages used with npx launcher
+//
+// # Validation Pattern: External Registry Check
+//
+// NPM package validation queries the npm registry using the npm CLI:
+//   - Uses `npm view <package> name` to check package existence
+//   - Returns hard errors if packages don't exist (unlike pip validation)
+//   - Requires npm to be installed on the system
+//
+// # When to Add Validation Here
+//
+// Add validation to this file when:
+//   - It validates Node.js/npm ecosystem packages
+//   - It checks npm registry package existence
+//   - It validates npx launcher packages
+//   - It validates Node.js version compatibility
+//
+// For package extraction functions, see npm.go.
+// For general validation, see validation.go.
+// For detailed documentation, see specs/validation-architecture.md
+package workflow
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"os"
+	"os/exec"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/githubnext/gh-aw/pkg/console"
+	"github.com/githubnext/gh-aw/pkg/logger"
+)
+
+var npmValidationLog = logger.New("workflow:npm_validation")
+
+// validateNpxPackages validates that npx packages are available on npm registry
+func (c *Compiler) validateNpxPackages(workflowData *WorkflowData) error {
+	packages := extractNpxPackages(workflowData)
+	if len(packages) == 0 {
+		npmValidationLog.Print("No npx packages to validate")
+		return nil
+	}
+
+	npmValidationLog.Printf("Validating %d npx packages", len(packages))
+
+	// Check if npm is available
+	_, err := exec.LookPath("npm")
+	if err != nil {
+		npmValidationLog.Print("npm command not found, cannot validate npx packages")
+		return fmt.Errorf("npm command not found - cannot validate npx packages. Install Node.js/npm or disable validation")
+	}
+
+	var errors []string
+	for _, pkg := range packages {
+		npmValidationLog.Printf("Validating npm package: %s", pkg)
+
+		// Use npm view to check if package exists
+		cmd := exec.Command("npm", "view", pkg, "name")
+		output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
+
+		if err != nil {
+			npmValidationLog.Printf("Package validation failed for %s: %v", pkg, err)
+			errors = append(errors, fmt.Sprintf("npx package '%s' not found on npm registry: %s", pkg, strings.TrimSpace(string(output))))
+		} else {
+			npmValidationLog.Printf("Package validated successfully: %s", pkg)
+			if c.verbose {
+				fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, console.FormatInfoMessage(fmt.Sprintf("✓ npm package validated: %s", pkg)))
+			}
+		}
+	}
+
+	if len(errors) > 0 {
+		npmValidationLog.Printf("npx package validation failed with %d errors", len(errors))
+		return fmt.Errorf("npx package validation failed:\n  - %s", strings.Join(errors, "\n  - "))
+	}
+
+	npmValidationLog.Print("All npx packages validated successfully")
+	return nil
+}

+# 🛠️ 管理 API
+
+**注意：以下内容适用于有一定技术能力的用户，否则请跳过此页面！！！**
+
+本文档说明如何直接调用 Metapi 管理后台的 `/api/*` 接口，用脚本完成站点与账号管理。
+
+[返回文档维护页](./README.md)
+
+[返回文档首页](/)
+
+---
+
+## 适用范围
+
+这组接口适合以下场景：
+
+- 初始化新实例，批量导入站点和账号
+- 用 Shell / Python / CI 脚本维护现有管理数据
+- 在外部系统里接入 Metapi 后台能力，而不是手工点页面
+
+> [!IMPORTANT]
+> 本页介绍的是 **管理 API**，不是下游客户端调用的 `/v1/*` 代理接口。
+> - 管理 API 使用 `AUTH_TOKEN`
+> - 代理接口使用 `PROXY_TOKEN`
+
+## 认证方式
+
+所有受保护的管理接口都需要携带：
+
+```http
+Authorization: Bearer <AUTH_TOKEN>
+```
+
+其中：
+
+- `AUTH_TOKEN` 就是你启动 Metapi 时配置的管理员令牌
+- 如果你后来在「设置」里修改过管理员令牌，脚本里也要同步改成新值
+- 管理端如果启用了 `ADMIN_IP_ALLOWLIST`，脚本调用方的来源 IP 也必须命中白名单
+
+管理 API 不需要额外先调用“登录接口”；脚本直接带 `AUTH_TOKEN` 即可。
+
+推荐先准备两个环境变量：
+
+```bash
+export METAPI_ADMIN_BASE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:4000"
+# 或者
+# export METAPI_ADMIN_BASE_URL="https://your-domain.com"
+export METAPI_AUTH_TOKEN="your-admin-token"
+```
+
+之后所有请求都可以复用：
+
+```bash
+curl -sS "${METAPI_ADMIN_BASE_URL}/api/sites" \
+  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${METAPI_AUTH_TOKEN}"
+```
+
+## 通用约定
+
+| 项目 | 说明 |
+|------|------|
+| 接口前缀 | 管理接口统一在 `/api/*` |
+| 请求体 | 默认使用 `application/json` |
+| 认证方式 | `Authorization: Bearer <AUTH_TOKEN>` |
+| 成功判定 | 除了看 HTTP 状态码，也要看响应体里的 `success` / `error` / `message` |
+| 业务失败返回 | 有些接口会返回 `200`，但响应体里是 `success: false` |
+| 常见错误码 | `400` 参数错误、`401/403` 认证失败、`409` 资源冲突、`429` 触发限流 |
+
+> [!TIP]
+> 对脚本来说，最稳妥的做法是：
+> 1. 先检查 HTTP 状态码
+> 2. 再检查返回 JSON 里的 `success`、`error`、`message`
+> 3. 不要只靠 `200` 判断调用成功
+
+## 常用脚本流程
+
+脚本化添加一个新站点并绑定账号，通常按下面顺序：
+
+1. `POST /api/sites/detect` 自动识别平台
+2. `POST /api/sites` 创建站点
+3. `POST /api/accounts/verify-token` 验证凭证
+4. `POST /api/accounts` 保存账号
+
+最小流程示例：
+
+```bash
+# 1. 自动识别站点类型
+curl -sS "${METAPI_ADMIN_BASE_URL}/api/sites/detect" \
+  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${METAPI_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
+  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+  -d '{
+    "url": "https://api.example.com"
+  }'
+
+# 2. 创建站点
+curl -sS "${METAPI_ADMIN_BASE_URL}/api/sites" \
+  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${METAPI_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
+  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+  -d '{
+    "name": "My New API",
+    "url": "https://api.example.com",
+    "platform": "new-api"
+  }'
+
+# 3. 验证 API Key 或 Session Token
+curl -sS "${METAPI_ADMIN_BASE_URL}/api/accounts/verify-token" \
+  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${METAPI_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
+  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+  -d '{
+    "siteId": 1,
+    "accessToken": "sk-or-session-token",
+    "credentialMode": "apikey"
+  }'
+
+# 4. 保存账号
+curl -sS "${METAPI_ADMIN_BASE_URL}/api/accounts" \
+  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${METAPI_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
+  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+  -d '{
+    "siteId": 1,
+    "accessToken": "sk-or-session-token",
+    "credentialMode": "apikey"
+  }'
+```
+
+## 站点接口
+
+### 1. 获取站点列表
+
+`GET /api/sites`
+
+返回当前全部站点。响应除了站点自身字段，还会带上聚合出来的 `totalBalance` 和 `subscriptionSummary`。
+
+示例：
+
+```bash
+curl -sS "${METAPI_ADMIN_BASE_URL}/api/sites" \
+  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${METAPI_AUTH_TOKEN}"
+```
+
+示例响应：
+
+```json
+[
+  {
+    "id": 1,
+    "name": "My New API",
+    "url": "https://api.example.com",
+    "platform": "new-api",
+    "status": "active",
+    "useSystemProxy": false,

pr_title: Fix SQLite literal unions decoding
issue:
#### Issue #470: Embrace Effect Schema for table definitions (schema-first approach)

## Overview

Currently, LiveStore uses a **column-first approach** for table definitions where each column is defined separately with its own SQLite type and optionally refined with an Effect schema. This proposal suggests flipping to a **schema-first approach** where the entire table structure is defined using a single Effect schema, with SQLite-specific annotations added directly to schema properties as needed.

## Current Implementation (Column-First)

```typescript
const todos = State.SQLite.table({
  name: 'todos',
  columns: {
    id: State.SQLite.text({ primaryKey: true }),
    text: State.SQLite.text({ default: '' }),
    completed: State.SQLite.boolean({ default: false }),
    deletedAt: State.SQLite.integer({ nullable: true, schema: Schema.DateFromNumber }),
  },
})
```

**How it works:**
- Start with SQLite column type (`text`, `integer`, `boolean`, etc.)
- Optionally refine with Effect schema for validation/transformation
- Each column defined independently with its own constraints
- Final row type assembled from individual column definitions

## Proposed Implementation (Schema-First)

```typescript
const todos = State.SQLite.schemaTable({
  name: 'todos',
  schema: Schema.Struct({
    id: Schema.String.annotations({ 
      primaryKey: true 
    }),
    text: Schema.String.annotations({ 
      default: '' 
    }),
    completed: Schema.Boolean.annotations({ 
      default: false 
    }),
    deletedAt: Schema.optional(Schema.Date).annotations({ 
      sqlite: { columnType: 'integer' } // Store Date as integer timestamp
    }),
  }),
  constraints: {
    // Table-level constraints only
    indexes: [
      { name: 'idx_completed', columns: ['completed'] },
    ],
  },
})
```

**How it would work:**
- Start with Effect schema defining the complete data structure
- Use Effect Schema's built-in annotation system for column-level configuration
- Automatically infer SQLite column types from schema types
- Add SQLite-specific annotations only when needed
- Table-level constraints (indexes, multi-column constraints) go in separate `constraints` object

## Effect Schema Annotations

Leveraging Effect Schema's built-in annotation system for column configuration:

### Built-in Annotations (reused for SQLite)
- `default`: Default value for the column
- `title`: Column title/label
- `description`: Column documentation
- `examples`: Example values

### Custom SQLite Annotations
- `primaryKey`: Mark as primary key
- `nullable`: Allow null values (for optional fields)
- `sqlite`: SQLite-specific overrides

## Type Mapping

The system would automatically map Effect schema types to SQLite columns:

| Effect Schema Type | Default SQLite Column | Notes |
|-------------------|----------------------|-------|
| `Schema.String` | `text` | Direct mapping |
| `Schema.Number` | `real` | Floating point numbers |
| `Schema.Int` | `integer` | Integer numbers |
| `Schema.Boolean` | `integer` | 0/1 representation |
| `Schema.Date` | `text` | ISO string by default |
| `Schema.optional(T)` | `nullable: true` | Nullable columns |
| Complex objects | `text` + JSON | JSON serialization |

## SQLite-Specific Annotations

When the default mapping isn't suitable, use the `sqlite` annotation:

```typescript
const events = State.SQLite.schemaTable({
  name: 'events',
  schema: Schema.Struct({
    id: Schema.String.annotations({ primaryKey: true }),
    timestamp: Schema.Date.annotations({ 
      sqlite: { columnType: 'integer' } // Store Date as Unix timestamp
    }),
    data: Schema.Struct({ /* ... */ }).annotations({ 
      sqlite: { columnType: 'text' } // Store as JSON string
    }),
  }),
})
```

## Precedent: Client Documents

LiveStore already implements a schema-first approach for client documents:

```typescript
const uiState = State.SQLite.clientDocument({
  name: 'uiState',
  schema: Schema.Struct({ 
    newTodoText: Schema.String, 
    filter: Schema.Literal('all', 'active', 'completed') 
  }),
  default: { newTodoText: '', filter: 'all' },
})
```

This demonstrates that the infrastructure already exists to support schema-first table definitions.

## Benefits

### Developer Experience
- **Single source of truth**: Schema defines both TypeScript types and database structure
- **Better type inference**: Complete type safety from one schema definition
- **Reduced boilerplate**: Less repetitive column definitions
- **Consistency**: Aligns with Effect ecosystem patterns
- **Familiar annotation system**: Uses Effect Schema's existing annotation patterns

### Maintainability
- **Easier refactoring**: Change schema in one place
- **Clear data contracts**: Schema serves as documentation
- **Validation by default**: Built-in runtime validation from Effect schema

### Performance
- **Intelligent defaults**: Automatic optimal column type selection
- **Explicit control**: Override defaults when needed for performance
- **Index-friendly**: Easy to specify indexes on schema properties

## Examples

### Basic Usage
```typescript
const users = State.SQLite.schemaTable({
  name: 'users',
  schema: Schema.Struct({
    id: Schema.String.annotations({ primaryKey: true }),
    name: Schema.String.annotations({ default: '' }),
    email: Schema.String,
    age: Schema.optional(Schema.Int),
  }),
})
```

### Advanced Usage with Custom Types
```typescript
const Priority = Schema.Literal('low', 'medium', 'high')

const issues = State.SQLite.schemaTable({
  name: 'issues',
  schema: Schema.Struct({
    id: Schema.String.annotations({ primaryKey: true }),
    title: Schema.String,
    priority: Priority,
    createdAt: Schema.Date.annotations({ 
      sqlite: { columnType: 'integer' } // Unix timestamp
    }),
    metadata: Schema.Record(Schema.String, Schema.Unknown).annotations({ 
      sqlite: { columnType: 'text' } // JSON string
    }),
  }),
  constraints: {
    indexes: [
      { name: 'idx_priority', columns: ['priority'] },
      { name: 'idx_created', columns: ['createdAt'] },
    ],
  },
})
```

## Related Issues

- #382 - Effect 4 notes (parent issue)
- #468 - Make query builder pluggable (related to schema integration)
- #63 - Improved schema hashes (schema evolution considerations)

## Technical Implementation Notes

The implementation would likely:

1. Extend the existing DSL infrastructure in `packages/@livestore/common/src/schema/state/sqlite/db-schema/dsl/`
2. Add new functions alongside existing column definition functions
3. Reuse existing `ColumnDefinition` and `TableDefinition` types
4. Leverage the client document implementation patterns
5. Use Effect Schema's annotation system for column-level configuration
6. Maintain backward compatibility with existing column-first approach

This approach provides a more idiomatic Effect-based API while maintaining the performance and flexibility of the current system.

Specifically, if the Agent's first retry produces a result that fails Pydantic validation (e.g., malformed JSON), the system crashes immediately. This prevents the task from proceeding to subsequent retry attempts, effectively making the max retries limit always "1" in failure scenarios.   

Of course, the probability of the agent failing to meet the requirements of output_pydantic in two consecutive executions is very low, but it shouldn't be zero. This is just my humble opinion.

1. Set up a Task with output_pydantic=SomeModel and guardrail_max_retries=3.

4. Observe that the process terminates with a Pydantic error after the first retry, instead of attempting 3 retries as configured.

#### Issue #345: Add support for `[start:end]` slice syntax

 ### Summary

 Add support for `[start:end]` slice syntax that allows extracting subsequences from arrays, similar to Python's list slicing or jq's array slicing capabilities.

### Motivation

Currently, mq supports individual element access with `.[index]` and table cell access with `.[row][col]`, but lacks a convenient way to extract ranges of elements from arrays or lists. Adding slice syntax would provide a more intuitive and powerful way to work with sequences.

### Proposed Syntax

```bash
# Basic slice syntax
[1:3]    # Extract elements from index 1 to 3 (exclusive)
[0:5]    # Extract first 5 elements
[2:]     # Extract from index 2 to end
[:3]     # Extract first 3 elements
[:]      # Extract all elements (copy)
```

### Implementation Plan

#### 1. AST/Parser Changes
- **Location**: `crates/mq-lang/src/ast/parser.rs`
- **Action**: Extend parser to recognize `[start:end]` syntax
- **Details**:
 - Add colon token recognition if not already present
 - Extend `parse_selector_table_args()` or create new parsing method
 - Handle optional start/end indices (e.g., `[:3]`, `[2:]`)

#### 2. AST Node Definition
- **Location**: `crates/mq-lang/src/ast/node.rs`
- **Action**: Add slice representation to AST
- **Options**:
 - Extend `Selector` enum with new `Slice(Option<usize>, Option<usize>)` variant
 - Or add new expression type if slicing should be a first-class operation

#### 3. Lexer Updates
- **Location**: `crates/mq-lang/src/lexer.rs`
- **Action**: Ensure colon token (`:`) is properly tokenized
- **Details**: May already exist, but verify TokenKind includes colon

#### 4. Evaluation Logic
- **Location**: `crates/mq-lang/src/eval/`
- **Action**: Implement slice semantics
- **Details**:
 - Handle bounds checking
 - Support negative indices (if desired)
 - Ensure consistent behavior with existing array/list operations

#### 5. Integration with Existing Features
- **Compatibility**: Ensure slice syntax works with:
 - Array literals: `[1,2,3,4,5] | [1:3]`
 - List selectors: `.[] | nodes | [1:3]`
 - Nested operations: `[1:3] | [0]`

### Technical Considerations

1. **Bounds Handling**:
  - Should use 0-based indexing (consistent with existing `.[index]`)
  - End index should be exclusive (common convention)
  - Out-of-bounds indices should be clamped or return appropriate errors

2. **AST Design Decision**:
  - Whether to treat slicing as a selector operation (like `.[index]`) or as a distinct expression type
  - Consider reusing existing range operator (`..`) concepts if applicable

3. **Error Handling**:
  - Use `miette` crate for user-friendly error messages
  - Handle invalid ranges (e.g., `[5:2]` where start > end)

### Testing Requirements

- Unit tests for parser changes
- Integration tests for slice operations
- Edge case testing (empty ranges, out-of-bounds, negative indices)
- Compatibility tests with existing array/list operations

### Related Code Locations

**Key files to modify:**
- `crates/mq-lang/src/ast/parser.rs` - Add slice parsing logic
- `crates/mq-lang/src/ast/node.rs` - Add slice AST node
- `crates/mq-lang/src/lexer.rs` - Ensure colon token support
- `crates/mq-lang/src/eval/` - Add slice evaluation

**Reference implementations:**
- Existing `.[index]` syntax in `parse_selector_table_args()`
- Array parsing in `parse_array()`
- Range operator (`..`) implementation for inspiration

This feature would significantly enhance mq's array and list manipulation capabilities while maintaining consistency with existing syntax patterns.

issue:
#### Issue #532: search misses matches in symlinked subdirectories when searching parent workspace root

## Summary

`probe search` does not traverse/find matches inside symlinked subdirectories when the search path is the **parent workspace root**.

Searching the symlink target path directly works. Searching the resolved real path works. Searching the parent directory that contains the symlink returns `No results found`.

This breaks workspace-root search in tools that expose multiple repos via symlinked project dirs.

## Version

Tested with `@probelabs/probe@0.6.0-rc300`.

## Minimal Reproduction

Run from a checkout with Probe installed.

```bash
TMP=/tmp/probe-symlink-repro
rm -rf "$TMP"
mkdir -p "$TMP/real/docs" "$TMP/ws"
cat > "$TMP/real/docs/config.mdx" <<'TXT'
Database storage support.
Set `audit.store_type` to `db`.
TXT
ln -s "$TMP/real/docs" "$TMP/ws/tyk-docs"
```

Control check:

```bash
rg -n "audit\.store_type" "$TMP/ws" "$TMP/ws/tyk-docs" "$TMP/real/docs"
```

Expected control output includes matches in:
- `/tmp/probe-symlink-repro/ws/tyk-docs/config.mdx`
- `/tmp/probe-symlink-repro/real/docs/config.mdx`

Now compare Probe behavior.

1. Search parent workspace root:

```bash
./node_modules/.bin/probe search '"audit.store_type"' "$TMP/ws" -o plain
```

Actual:
- `No results found.`

2. Search symlink path directly:

```bash
./node_modules/.bin/probe search '"audit.store_type"' "$TMP/ws/tyk-docs" -o plain
```

Actual:
- returns `config.mdx`

3. Search real path directly:

```bash
./node_modules/.bin/probe search '"audit.store_type"' "$TMP/real/docs" -o plain
```

Actual:
- returns `config.mdx`

## Expected Behavior

Searching the workspace root should recurse into symlinked project directories and return the same match that is visible when searching the symlink path or real path directly.

## Why this matters

This causes agent/search workflows that search from a workspace root containing symlinked repos to miss exact matches on the first query, then broaden/retry unnecessarily.

I reproduced this in a Visor workspace layout where multiple repos are exposed under a common root as symlinks, but the repro above does not depend on Visor.

#### Issue #533: delegated search fails with 'Delegate agent returned invalid response (not a string)' before raw-search fallback succeeds

## Summary

Delegated search can fail immediately with:

```text
Delegation failed: Delegate agent returned invalid response (not a string)
```

The parent search then falls back to raw search and succeeds.

This looks like a delegate response-shape mismatch rather than a search failure.

## Version

Tested with `@probelabs/probe@0.6.0-rc300`.

## Reproduction

From a checkout with Probe installed and `GOOGLE_API_KEY` set:

```bash
DOCS=$(find /home/buger/projects/REFINE/Oel/.visor/worktrees/worktrees -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'TykTechnologies-tyk-docs-main-*' | sort | tail -1)

timeout 40 ./node_modules/.bin/probe agent \
  'Find where audit.store_type is used in the configuration.' \
  --path "$DOCS" \
  --prompt code-searcher \
  --provider google \
  --model gemini-2.5-flash \
  --allowed-tools search,extract,listFiles \
  --allow-edit \
  --max-iterations 4 \
  2>&1
```

## Actual Behavior

The run logs this failure during delegated search:

```text
Delegated search failed, falling back to raw search: Error: Delegation failed: Delegate agent returned invalid response (not a string)
    at delegate (.../node_modules/@probelabs/probe/build/delegate.js:711:9)
```

The debug output shows the delegate path rejects non-string responses here:

- `node_modules/@probelabs/probe/src/delegate.js:621-623`

```js
if (typeof response !== 'string') {
  throw new Error('Delegate agent returned invalid response (not a string)');
}
```

After the failure, raw search runs and succeeds, and the overall agent still produces valid targets.

## Expected Behavior

Delegated search should accept the subagent result shape that Probe itself produces in this path, or normalize it before validation, so it does not fail and fall back unnecessarily.

## Why this matters

This adds avoidable latency/noise to delegated search and can obscure real search behavior with fallback behavior.

#### Issue #534: search.delegate subagents do not inherit allowEdit/hashLines from parent agent

## Summary

When a parent Probe agent runs with `allowEdit=true`, delegated search subagents do **not** inherit that state, so they also do not inherit `hashLines=true`.

This matters because `ProbeAgent` derives `hashLines` from `allowEdit` by default:

- `allowEdit = !!options.allowEdit`
- `hashLines = options.hashLines !== undefined ? !!options.hashLines : this.allowEdit`

However, the `search.delegate` path constructs the delegate call without passing either `allowEdit` or `hashLines`, so the delegated `code-searcher` subagent runs with:

- `Allow Edit: false`
- `Hash Lines: false`

## Version

Tested with `@probelabs/probe@0.6.0-rc300`.

## Evidence in code

Parent agent defaults:
- `node_modules/@probelabs/probe/src/agent/ProbeAgent.js:211-212`

```js
this.allowEdit = !!options.allowEdit;
this.hashLines = options.hashLines !== undefined ? !!options.hashLines : this.allowEdit;
```

Generic delegate helper supports inheritance when passed:
- `node_modules/@probelabs/probe/src/delegate.js:488-490`

```js
enableBash,
bashConfig,
allowEdit,
```

But `search.delegate` does not pass it:
- `node_modules/@probelabs/probe/src/tools/vercel.js:532-547`

```js
const runDelegation = () => delegate({
  task: delegateTask,
  ...
  enableBash: false,
  bashConfig: null,
  promptType: 'code-searcher',
  allowedTools: ['search', 'extract', 'listFiles'],
  searchDelegate: false,
  schema: CODE_SEARCH_SCHEMA,
})
```

## Reproduction

With `GOOGLE_API_KEY` set:

```bash
DOCS=$(find /home/buger/projects/REFINE/Oel/.visor/worktrees/worktrees -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'TykTechnologies-tyk-docs-main-*' | sort | tail -1)

timeout 40 ./node_modules/.bin/probe agent \
  'Find where audit.store_type is used in the configuration.' \
  --path "$DOCS" \
  --prompt code-searcher \
  --provider google \
  --model gemini-2.5-flash \
  --allowed-tools search,extract,listFiles \
  --allow-edit \
  --max-iterations 4 \
  2>&1
```

## Actual Behavior

Top-level agent logs:

```text
[DEBUG] Allow Edit: true
[DEBUG] Hash Lines: true
```

Delegated search subagent logs:

```text
[DEBUG] Allow Edit: false
[DEBUG] Hash Lines: false
```

## Expected Behavior

If the parent agent has `allowEdit=true`, delegated search subagents should inherit the same edit/hash-line state unless explicitly overridden.

At minimum, the `search.delegate` path should pass through `allowEdit` and `hashLines` consistently with the parent agent state.

## Scope note

This is not a claim that read-only searchers should always use hash lines. The issue is specifically inconsistent inheritance: the parent is in edit/hash mode, but the delegated subagent silently loses that mode.

pr_title: fix: Allow organization owners to delete organizations with soft-delete cascade
issue:
#### Issue #3517: Allow organization owners to delete organizations with soft-delete cascade

## Summary

Organization owners should be able to delete organizations they own. Deletion must cascade through all owned resources using soft deletes so that the existing canvases cleaner can process them, and a grace period should be enforced before permanent removal.

## Requested work

- Add an API endpoint (and corresponding protobuf definition) for deleting an organization.
- Enforce RBAC: only users with the **owner** role on the organization may trigger deletion.
- Soft-delete the organization record and all child resources, including but not limited to:
  - Canvases (so the canvases cleaner picks them up)
  - Components, triggers, and edges belonging to those canvases
  - Organization memberships / invitations
  - Any other org-scoped resources (API keys, secrets, integrations, etc.)
- Implement a **grace period of ~30 days** before hard deletion, allowing potential recovery.
- Audit and document the full list of resources that must be cascade-deleted.
- Surface the delete action in the React UI (`web_src/`) with an appropriate confirmation flow (e.g., type-to-confirm dialog).
- Add tests covering:
  - Permission checks (non-owners are rejected).
  - Soft-delete propagation to all child resources.
  - Canvases cleaner correctly processes soft-deleted canvases from an org deletion.
  - Grace-period expiry and final hard deletion.

## SuperPlane context

- Canvases are the core workflow primitive; their soft-delete path already exists for the canvases cleaner. Organization deletion should reuse this mechanism rather than introduce a parallel cleanup pipeline.
- RBAC roles are already modeled in the backend (`pkg/`); the owner permission check should align with the existing role system.
- Protobuf changes in `protos/` will be needed for the new RPC, and the Go service layer in `pkg/` / `cmd/` will implement the business logic.

## Notes

- The exact grace period (30 days is suggested) should be confirmed during implementation; consider making it configurable via an environment variable or organization setting.
- Consider emitting an event when an organization enters the soft-deleted state so other integrations or notifications can react.
- Edge cases to handle: what happens if the last owner tries to delete the org while other members still exist? Decide whether to require removing all members first or cascade-remove memberships automatically.

pr_title: Generic guardrail api update
issue:
#### Issue #19363: Migrate Pillar Security guardrail to Generic Guardrail API

## Overview

Migrate the Pillar Security guardrail integration from the dedicated `guardrail: pillar` type to the `guardrail: generic_guardrail_api` approach.

## Background

The Generic Guardrail API was introduced in #17175 to allow guardrail providers to integrate with LiteLLM without requiring PRs to the repository. We have contributed several improvements to make this API production-ready:

- #17175: Generic Guardrail API introduction
- #18647: Generic guardrail API updates
- #18932: SerializationIterator fix and tools support
- #19023: Clean error messages for blocked requests

## Migration

**Before (dedicated guardrail):**
```yaml
guardrails:
  - guardrail_name: "pillar-security"
    litellm_params:
      guardrail: pillar
      mode: pre_call
      api_key: os.environ/PILLAR_API_KEY
      api_base: os.environ/PILLAR_API_BASE
```

**After (generic API):**
```yaml
guardrails:
  - guardrail_name: "pillar-security"
    litellm_params:
      guardrail: generic_guardrail_api
      mode: [pre_call, post_call]
      api_base: https://api.pillar.security/api/v1/integrations/litellm
      api_key: os.environ/PILLAR_API_KEY
      additional_provider_specific_params:
        plr_mask: true
        plr_evidence: true
        plr_scanners: true
```

## Tasks

- [x] Update `pillar_security.md` documentation - #19362
- [x] Add Pillar example to `generic_guardrail_api.md` - #19362
- [x] Add Pillar to `quick_start.md` examples - #19362
- [ ] Deprecate dedicated pillar guardrail code (future)

## Related PR

- #19362

---

#### Issue #19365: docs: Migrate Pillar Security to Generic Guardrail API

## Description

Migrate Pillar Security integration documentation to use the `generic_guardrail_api` instead of the dedicated `pillar` guardrail type. 

This migration aligns with the Generic Guardrail API specification that was introduced in previous contributions to LiteLLM.

## Changes

- Updated `pillar_security.md` to use `generic_guardrail_api` configuration format
- Added Pillar Security as a real-world example in `generic_guardrail_api.md`
- Added Pillar Security to the guardrails examples in `quick_start.md`

## Related PRs

- #17175 - Initial Generic Guardrail API
- #18647 - Add structured_messages parameter
- #18932 - Add tools and tool_calls parameters
- #19023 - Support model parameter for guardrails

## Resolution

PR: #19364

pr_title: fix(security): prevent path traversal in checkpoint_dir and save_to_file
issue:
#### Issue #110: Potential Path Traversal in checkpoint_dir leading to unintended file write

### Description
I noticed a potential path handling issue related to checkpoint saving in the ACE framework.
Specifically, the checkpoint_dir parameter provided to OfflineACE.run() is used to construct file paths without normalization or validation.

### Affected Code Paths
```
ace/adaptation.py → OfflineACE.run()
ace/skillbook.py → Skillbook.save_to_file()
```
Relevant implementation:
```
file_path = Path(path)
file_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
with file_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
```
### Issue
The provided path is not normalized or restricted to a base directory. This means that directory traversal sequences such as:
```
../
```
may allow writing files outside the intended checkpoint directory.
In other words, the expected boundary:
```
<checkpoint_dir>/*
```
can be bypassed, resulting in writes to arbitrary locations on the filesystem.

### Impact
This could result in files being written to unintended locations on the filesystem, depending on how checkpoint_dir is supplied in downstream applications.

### Suggested Mitigation
One possible mitigation could be to normalize and validate the target path before writing:

- Resolve the path using `Path.resolve()`
- Ensure the resolved path remains within an intended base directory
- Reject paths containing traversal sequences (e.g., "../") if not explicitly supported

For example, enforcing that all checkpoint files stay within a designated directory may help prevent unintended file writes.

### Question
Is this behavior intentional (i.e., allowing arbitrary output paths), or should checkpoint_dir be restricted to a specific base directory?
If not intended, adding path normalization (e.g., Path.resolve()) and boundary checks may help prevent directory traversal.

### Additional Note
I verified this behavior against the latest version of the repository, and it appears to still be present.
Happy to provide more details if helpful.

Thanks!

+"""Path safety utilities — prevent directory traversal in file writes."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def safe_resolve(path: str | Path) -> Path:
+    """Resolve a path and reject directory-traversal sequences.
+
+    Uses ``os.path.realpath`` to normalise the path, then verifies that no
+    ``..`` component survived resolution.  This prevents writes to unintended
+    locations when the caller-supplied *path* contains traversal sequences
+    such as ``../``.
+
+    Raises:
+        ValueError: If the resolved path still contains ``..`` components.
+    """
+    resolved = Path(os.path.realpath(path))
+    # After realpath, ".." should be gone.  Belt-and-suspenders check:
+    if ".." in resolved.parts:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Path traversal detected: resolved path {resolved} "
+            f"still contains '..' components."
+        )
+    return resolved
+
+
+def safe_resolve_within(path: str | Path, base_dir: str | Path) -> Path:
+    """Resolve *path* and ensure it stays within *base_dir*.
+
+    Both *path* and *base_dir* are normalised via :func:`safe_resolve`
+    before the containment check.
+
+    Raises:
+        ValueError: If the resolved *path* escapes *base_dir*.
+    """
+    resolved_base = safe_resolve(base_dir)
+    resolved_path = safe_resolve(path)
+    try:
+        resolved_path.relative_to(resolved_base)
+    except ValueError:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Path traversal detected: {resolved_path} is not inside "
+            f"the expected base directory {resolved_base}."
+        ) from None
+    return resolved_path

### Feature Area

Agent capabilities

### Is your feature request related to a an existing bug? Please link it here.

Currently, setting `allow_delegation = True` lets the agent delegate the task to all the agents specified in the crew.

#### Issue #1367: Feature / Question: go-tree-sitter dependency

### Feature / Question: go-tree-sitter dependency

Hi team,  

I noticed that the project currently uses `github.com/smacker/go-tree-sitter` for syntax tree parsing. Since `go-tree-sitter` relies on CGO, cross-platform compilation (especially for darwin/arm64) becomes complicated.  

I have a few questions:  
1. Is `go-tree-sitter` strictly required for Katana, or only for certain features?  
2. Are there any alternative pure-Go libraries we could use instead of `go-tree-sitter` to simplify cross-platform builds?  

This would help in making snapshot builds and CI/CD pipelines simpler, without needing to configure CGO or cross-compilers.  

Thanks!

---

### Use Case

- Simplifying cross-platform builds (Windows → macOS/ARM)  
- Avoiding CGO-related compilation issues  
- Maintaining full functionality while reducing dependency complexity

+"""Guard against reintroducing deprecated setuptools resource APIs."""
+
+import subprocess
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+
+
+def test_no_deprecated_setuptools_resource_api_usage():
+    """Fail when deprecated setuptools resource APIs appear in tracked Python files."""
+    deprecated_api = "_".join(["pkg", "resources"])
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        ["git", "grep", "-n", deprecated_api, "--", "*.py"],
+        cwd=REPO_ROOT,
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+        check=False,
+    )
+
+    assert result.returncode in (0, 1), f"git grep failed:\n{result.stderr}"
+    assert result.returncode == 1, (
+        "Found deprecated setuptools resource API usage in Python files:\n"
+        f"{result.stdout}"
+    )

issue:
#### Issue #67333: planner: nil pointer dereference when tidb_enforce_mpp keeps a missing TiFlash path

## Bug Report

Suggested labels: `type/bug`, `sig/planner`, `component/tiflash`, `severity/moderate`, `affects-8.5`, `affects-9.0`

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

```sql
create table t(a int, b int, c int, primary key(a));
create table t2(a int, b int);
insert into t values(1,2,3), (4,5,6);
alter table t set tiflash replica 1;

set @@sql_mode = '';
set @@tidb_isolation_read_engines = 'tidb,tikv';
set @@tidb_allow_mpp = 1;
set @@tidb_enforce_mpp = 1;

explain insert into t2 select a, b from t where a in (1, 2);
```

`insert into t2 select a, b from t where a in (1, 2);` also hits the same planner panic, but `EXPLAIN` is enough to reproduce it because the panic happens during plan building.

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

The statement should be planned successfully.

TiDB should either:

- choose a non-TiFlash path, or
- return a normal warning that MPP/TiFlash cannot be used under the current isolation-read setting.

It should not panic.

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

TiDB panics during planning with:

```text
ERROR 1105 (HY000): runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
```

The stack points to `generateOtherIndexMerge()`:

```text
github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/planner/core.generateOtherIndexMerge
github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/planner/core.generateIndexMergePath
github.com/pingcap/tidb/pkg/planner/core.deriveStats4DataSource
```

pr_title: fix: FastAPI 0.132.0 compatibility (content-type and ORJSONResponse)
issue:
#### Issue #21301: Upgrading Prefect server to 3.6.19+ breaks older clients (< 3.6.19) with 422 on POST /task_runs/

  ### Description

  PR #20822 upgraded FastAPI from 0.128.0 to 0.132.0 and changed the client's `create_task_run` to send `json=` instead of `content=`. However, no server-side backward compatibility was added. Since the server's FastAPI pin is
  `>=0.111.0,<1.0.0`, any server upgrade to 3.6.19+ pulls in FastAPI 0.132+, which rejects the old client's request body with a 422.

  The root cause is that httpx's `content=` parameter (used by the old client) sends the body **without a `Content-Type` header**, which old FastAPI tolerated but FastAPI 0.132.0 does not.

  ### Reproduction

  ~~~python
  import httpx
  import json

  # Simulates what the old client (<3.6.19) does in create_task_run
  task_run_data = {
      "flow_run_id": "4d647261-5d2f-429c-8b66-a5fc39a505e8",
      "task_key": "my-task-key",
      "dynamic_key": "0",
  }

  # Old client uses content= (no Content-Type header)
  response = httpx.post(
      "http://<prefect-server>:4200/api/task_runs/",
      content=json.dumps(task_run_data),
  )
  print(response.status_code)  # 422
  print(response.json())
  # {'exception_message': 'Invalid request received.',
  #  'exception_detail': [{'type': 'model_attributes_type', 'loc': ['body'],
  #   'msg': 'Input should be a valid dictionary or object to extract fields from', ...}]}

  # New client uses json= (sets Content-Type: application/json) — works fine
  response = httpx.post(
      "http://<prefect-server>:4200/api/task_runs/",
      json=task_run_data,
  )
  print(response.status_code)  # 201
  ~~~

  ### Stack Trace

  ~~~
  prefect.exceptions.PrefectHTTPStatusError: Client error '422 Unprocessable Entity' for url 'http://prefect-server.prefect-dev.svc.cluster.local:4200/api/task_runs/'
  Response: {'exception_message': 'Invalid request received.', 'exception_detail': [{'type': 'model_attributes_type', 'loc': ['body'], 'msg': 'Input should be a valid dictionary or object to extract fields from', 'input':
  '{"state":{"type":"PENDING","name":"Pending",...}'}]}
  ~~~

  Full traceback originates from `prefect/client/orchestration/__init__.py` line 834:
  ~~~python
  response = await self._client.post("/task_runs/", content=content)
  ~~~

  ### Details

  - **Client version:** 3.5.0 (affects all clients <3.6.19)
  - **Server version:** 3.6.19+ (any version containing PR #20822)
  - **FastAPI version on server:** 0.132.0
  - **Affected endpoint:** `POST /task_runs/` (the only endpoint that used `content=` instead of `json=`)
  - **Introduced by:** https://github.com/PrefectHQ/prefect/pull/20822

  ### Suggested Fix

  Add server-side middleware to default `Content-Type: application/json` when the header is missing on POST/PUT/PATCH requests. This is a ~10 line change in `src/prefect/server/api/server.py`. I have a working fix with a regression test at
  https://github.com/chuqCTC/prefect/tree/fix/fastapi-content-type-backward-compat.

pr_title: fix: Add timeout to detect backend unavailability
issue:
#### Issue #378: [FEAT] Frontend connection status indicator doesn't update when backend becomes unavailable

## Description
The connection status indicator at the top of the UI remains green and shows "Connected" even when the backend server is shut down or becomes unavailable.

## Expected Behavior
When the backend server becomes unavailable (e.g., container stopped, network issues), the connection status should update to show "Disconnected" within a reasonable timeframe (5-10 seconds).

## Current Behavior
- Status indicator stays green showing "Connected"
- No visual feedback that the backend is unavailable
- Users may attempt actions that will fail without understanding why

## Root Cause Analysis
The `checkConnectionStatus` function in `App.tsx` (line 1135) does have proper error handling in the catch block (lines 1207-1212) that should set status to 'disconnected'. However, when the server shuts down:
- The fetch request in `authFetch` may be hanging/timing out
- The catch block isn't executing quickly enough to provide timely feedback

## Suggested Fix
Add aggressive timeout handling to fetch requests:
1. Add a timeout wrapper to `authFetch` utility (default 5-10 seconds)
2. Use AbortController to cancel hanging requests
3. Ensure the 5-second polling interval can detect backend unavailability within 2-3 cycles

## Related Code
- `src/App.tsx`: `checkConnectionStatus` function (lines 1135-1213)
- `src/services/auth.ts`: `authFetch` utility
- Polling interval: Every 5 seconds (line 985)

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start the application with backend running
2. Verify connection status shows "Connected" (green)
3. Stop the Docker container: `docker compose down`
4. Observe that status indicator remains green/connected
5. Expected: Should update to disconnected within ~10 seconds

## Priority
Medium - UX improvement, doesn't affect functionality but could confuse users
